correctness.rationale: The endomorphism matrix is necessarily (A,0; psi,mu) because the commutator ideal is Kz. Bracket preservation is A^T diag(1,lambda) A=mu diag(1,lambda); idempotence gives A^2=A, mu in {0,1}, psi A+mu psi=psi. If mu=1, invertibility forces A=I and psi=0. If mu=0, the image of A is totally isotropic, so anisotropy yields only 0 and I; in the split case the two distinct isotropic lines each contribute q choices of complement/kernel and q central lifts. Distinct rank-one projections on the same isotropic line never commute. Across the two isotropic lines they commute exactly when opposite lines are their kernels, yielding K_(q,q) plus 2q(q-1) isolates. The complete clique, centralizer, maximal-subsemigroup and commuting-probability formulas follow by counting graph vertices/edges. Independent enumeration directly multiplied idempotent matrices at q=3 and q=5, checking 18 and 50 noncentral vertices and q^2 edges respectively; source code also covers prime and F9 fields. The proof, not finite tests, supports arbitrary characteristic not 2 and all odd q.
